Topic: Someone in Northern Ireland loses £250,000 to an AI deepfake investment scam
Caption Notes:
Someone in Northern Ireland lost £250,000 to a scam that started with an AI-generated video of a well-known finance personality.

The video was only the hook. The rest happened on WhatsApp and on a laptop the scammers took control of.

4 warning signs:
1. A famous face promoting an investment
2. A small first payment, then pressure to pay more
3. The chat moves to WhatsApp
4. Someone asks for remote access to your computer

Spot one? Stop. Check the firm on the FCA register before you send a penny.

Police say a celebrity endorsement never proves an investment is real. Send this to someone who'd trust that video.

Source: PSNI, 7 Sep 2026.

Topic: UK small business AI use has more than doubled this year, to 47%
Caption Notes:
47% of UK small business owners now use AI. A year ago it was 22%.

Writing content, solving problems and coming up with ideas top the list. The confidence lags behind: fewer than 1 in 5 feel very confident using it, and security worries hold plenty back.

Using AI but not sure you're doing it right? Our starter guides cover the basics. Link in bio.

Source: Simply Business SME Insights Report 2026, survey of 1,842 UK small business owners.

Topic: Nearly half of UK adults find it harder to tell what's genuine online, NTS warns
Caption Notes:
Nearly half of UK adults (47%) say it’s getting harder to tell what’s genuine online. As AI grows, almost a quarter (24%) feel overwhelmed by how sophisticated scams have become.

National Trading Standards has published an AI Scam Watchlist of the top five AI-powered tricks: fake websites, voice cloning, deepfake video, AI-generated images and ‘digital humans’.

Bad spelling and blurry photos used to give scams away. They don’t anymore. Stop and think before you pay or share anything. Check the caller, website or message through a separate route, even if an AI search result says it’s real. Send no money and share no details until you’re confident.

Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI updates.

Source: National Trading Standards, 30 Sep 2026.

Topic: ChatGPT will show picture ads while it makes your images, US test first
Caption Notes:
ChatGPT is about to show picture ads while it makes your images. OpenAI announced the new format on 5 October. Testing starts later this month in the US, for people on the Free and Go plans.

In the UK, Free and Go users already see text ads under some answers. They arrived in June. Plus and Pro stay ad-free, and OpenAI says it shows no ads to under-18s.

OpenAI says ads never change ChatGPT's answers and advertisers never see your chats. You still decide how much the ads know about you:

• Open Settings > Ads controls. Switch off personalised ads, and stop past chats and memory shaping them.
• Use Temporary Chat for anything private. It shows no ads.
• On Free, you can go ads-free. The catch: fewer messages and no image making.

Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI updates.

Source: OpenAI, 5 Oct 2026.

Topic: Free Gemini drops to Flash-Lite only from 9 October
Caption Notes:
Free Gemini is shrinking. From 9 October, personal accounts without a Google AI plan only get Flash-Lite, Google's smallest model. Flash and Pro need a subscription.

AI Plus keeps Flash-Lite and Flash but loses Pro. Google will email Plus subscribers with their date. AI Pro and AI Ultra keep all three models, plus Deep Think.

Every model also gets an effort setting: low, medium or high. High gives fuller answers but eats your usage limit faster.

Google hasn't said which countries get the change, and its help page lists no exceptions. Check your model picker after 9 October.

• Update the Gemini app.
• Try Flash-Lite on your usual tasks before you pay.
• Upgrading? You can change or cancel a plan at any time.

Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI updates.

Source: Google Gemini Apps Help, 7 Oct 2026.

Topic: Google opens its SynthID AI detector to everyone
Caption Notes:
Not sure if that photo, video or voice note is real? Google has opened its SynthID Detector to everyone, worldwide, in English.

Upload a file at synthid.com and it checks for hidden watermarks left by AI from Google, OpenAI, NVIDIA and Kakao. Apple support is coming soon.

Treat the result as one clue. No watermark doesn’t prove a file is real. Another AI tool could still have made it.

You can also upload a file in the Gemini app and ask if Google AI made or edited it.

• Check suspicious media before you share it.
• No watermark? Still call back on a number you know.

Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI updates.

Source: Google, 7 Oct 2026.

Topic: UK watchdog gets 10 AI firms to explain how they train on your data
Caption Notes:
The UK’s data watchdog has pushed ten AI companies to change how they explain and protect the personal data used to train their AI.

The Information Commissioner’s Office named Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Stability AI. They have made changes or promised them: clearer information on how your data gets used, better help with your data rights and tougher checks on safeguards.

Apple, Cohere and OpenAI already publish separate privacy notices for model training.

The ICO now has AI agents in its sights. It has asked OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta about recent tests where agents got around their protections.

• Use ChatGPT? Read OpenAI’s model training privacy notice.
• Business using AI agents? The ICO wants your views by 20 November.

Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI updates.

Source: Information Commissioner’s Office, 8 Oct 2026.
